title: Naturality and substitution coherence of recursive counit comparisons
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For finite typed expressions $P$ with input locations and constructors input, coefficient unit, tensor and scheme pullback [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], let $S_P$ evaluate in $T,F,U$ on normalized inputs, and let $K_P$ evaluate in $\widehat T,\widehat F,\mathcal LU$ on their limits. Define $\beta_P:K_P\to\mathcal L S_P$ recursively by identities at inputs and units, $\beta_{T(P,Q)}=\beta_T(S_P,S_Q)\circ\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_Q)$ and $\beta_{F_f(P)}=\beta_F(S_P)\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_P)$. Here the primitive maps are those of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]: the defining quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L T(e_A,e_N)$ and $\mathcal L F_f(e_C)$, respectively. Put $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_P)$.

Assume $T,F,U$ preserve normalization and the specified primitive comparisons are natural isomorphisms. The recursive comparisons are natural in every input system: for a componentwise family $v_i:A_i\to A'_i$ between normalized inputs,
$$\beta_P(A')K_P(\mathcal L v)=\mathcal L(S_P(v))\beta_P(A).$$
Here $K_P(\mathcal L v)$ is the morphism obtained by functorial completed evaluation. The reduction comparisons $\gamma_P$ are natural as whole-system maps as well.

For any well-typed family of expressions $H_i$ substituted simultaneously for the input slots of an outer expression $P$, let $d:S_{P[H]}\xrightarrow{\sim}S_P(S_H)$ and $c:K_{P[H]}\xrightarrow{\sim}K_P(K_H)$ be the parenthesis-preserving evaluation/substitution identifications, recursively identities at leaves and images of the child identifications at tensor and pullback vertices. Then
$$\mathcal L(d)\,\beta_{P[H]}=\beta_P(S_H)\,K_P(\beta_{H_i})\,c.$$
The corresponding reduction equation is $d\,\gamma_{P[H]}=\gamma_P(S_H)\,\mathcal R(K_P(\beta_{H_i})c)$. These formulas include unit-only expressions and repeated input slots. In the induction on the outer expression, at a leaf the equation is identity, at a tensor vertex the two child squares compose with naturality of $T(e,e)$, and at a pullback vertex the child square composes with naturality of $F(e)$. The replacement $\mathcal R\mathcal L S_{H_i}\xrightarrow{e_{S_{H_i}}}S_{H_i}$ moves through each child comparison by $e_{S'}\mathcal R\mathcal L(u)=u e_S$; hence the flattened recursion and the iterated recursion use the same morphism, not just isomorphic endpoints.

Moreover, for any natural whole-system structural maps between expressions whose completed maps satisfy $\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$ and $\gamma_Q\mathcal R(\widehat a)=a\gamma_P$, these equations persist under identities, inverse maps, composition, tensoring with other expressions, pullback, and the same simultaneous substitution. This applies in particular to total-complex tensor constraints and finite adjunction-normalized pullback compositors once their primitive equations have been established. No equality of arbitrary derived morphisms is detected by evaluation.

proof.text: Use right-to-left composition throughout and suppress scheme subscripts only when the output types determine them. The expression definition supplies structural induction on a finite typed tree; a repeated input is evaluated by the same input object and map at every occurrence. The assumed closure under $T,F,U$ makes every $S_P$ normalized. The displayed recursion defines $K_P,S_P$ on morphisms as well as objects: at an input use its map, at a unit use the identity, and at a vertex apply its functor to the child maps. Applying the identity and composition laws of that functor proves the evaluation laws by induction. There is no reordering of tensor factors or alteration of parentheses in this recursion.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: typed expression induction and evaluation on maps

proof.text:
Abbreviate the specified primitive comparisons by $b_T,b_F$. The primitive lemma states, for maps of normalized systems $u:A\to A'$, $v:N\to N'$ and $w:C\to C'$,
$$b_T(A',N')\widehat T(\mathcal Lu,\mathcal Lv)=\mathcal L T(u,v)b_T(A,N),\qquad b_F(C')\widehat F_f(\mathcal Lw)=\mathcal L F_f(w)b_F(C).$$
It also gives the whole-system identity $e_{A'}\mathcal R\mathcal L(u)=u e_A$. These are naturality equations in the ordinary derived categories, not equations inferred by evaluation. Each primitive $b$ is invertible. Induction gives invertibility of every $\beta_P$: inputs and units give identities, and at each vertex apply the vertex functor to the inverses of the child comparisons, then compose with the inverse primitive comparison. The composites are inverses by the functor laws.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: the primitive naturality equations and recursive invertibility

proof.text: Prove the asserted input naturality by induction on $P$, writing $s_P=S_P(v)$ and $k_P=K_P(\mathcal Lv)$. At the input $i$, $\beta_P$ is the identity and $k_P=\mathcal L v_i=\mathcal Ls_P$. At a unit, both evaluations are constant functors on input families, their maps are identities and $\beta_P$ is the identity. Thus $\beta_P(A')k_P=\mathcal Ls_P\beta_P(A)$ holds in both base cases, including when there are no input slots.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: input naturality, the input and coefficient-unit cases

proof.text:
For the tensor case $P=T(X,Y)$ put $s_X=S_X(v)$ and $s_Y=S_Y(v)$. The induction hypotheses are $\beta_X(A')k_X=\mathcal Ls_X\beta_X(A)$ and the corresponding equation for $Y$. Expanding the left side and using these gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_P(A')k_P
&=b_T(S_X(A'),S_Y(A'))\widehat T(\beta_X(A')k_X,\beta_Y(A')k_Y)\\
&=b_T(S_X(A'),S_Y(A'))\widehat T(\mathcal Ls_X,\mathcal Ls_Y)\widehat T(\beta_X(A),\beta_Y(A))\\
&=\mathcal L T(s_X,s_Y)b_T(S_X(A),S_Y(A))\widehat T(\beta_X(A),\beta_Y(A))\\
&=\mathcal Ls_P\beta_P(A).
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality is precisely primitive naturality at the two child system maps. Both children are normalized by the hypothesis on the constructors.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: input naturality, tensor induction step

proof.text:
For $P=F_f(X)$, the child hypothesis and primitive pullback naturality give
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_P(A')k_P
&=b_F(S_X(A'))\widehat F_f(\beta_X(A')k_X)\\
&=b_F(S_X(A'))\widehat F_f(\mathcal Ls_X)\widehat F_f(\beta_X(A))\\
&=\mathcal L F_f(s_X)b_F(S_X(A))\widehat F_f(\beta_X(A))
=\mathcal Ls_P\beta_P(A).
\end{aligned}$$
Here the input and output categories of $\widehat F_f$ are respectively those of the source child on the target scheme of $f$ and of $P$ on its source scheme. Together with the preceding cases this proves naturality simultaneously for all input slots.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: input naturality, pullback induction step

proof.text:
Apply $\mathcal R$ to the naturality equation just proved, then postcompose with $e_{S_P(A')}$. For $s=S_P(v)$ counit naturality gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\gamma_P(A')\mathcal R(k_P)
&=e_{S_P(A')}\mathcal R(\beta_P(A')k_P)\\
&=e_{S_P(A')}\mathcal R\mathcal L(s)\mathcal R(\beta_P(A))
=s e_{S_P(A)}\mathcal R(\beta_P(A))
=s\gamma_P(A).
\end{aligned}$$
Every equality is already an equality of whole-system maps. This proves the requested naturality of $\gamma$, with no faithfulness claim about level evaluation.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: reduction naturality by the natural counit

proof.text:
Fix simultaneously all substituted expressions $H_i$ and their normalized inputs. Write $h_P=K_P(\beta_{H_i})c_P$, where $c_P:K_{P[H]}\to K_P(K_H)$, and write $d_P:S_{P[H]}\to S_P(S_H)$. Induct on the outer expression, with inductive assertion
$$\mathcal L(d_P)\beta_{P[H]}=\beta_P(S_H)h_P.$$
The parenthesis-preserving identifications are defined recursively: at a tensor $d_P=T(d_X,d_Y)$ and $c_P=\widehat T(c_X,c_Y)$, while at a pullback $d_P=F_f(d_X)$ and $c_P=\widehat F_f(c_X)$. Consequently $h_{T(X,Y)}=\widehat T(h_X,h_Y)$ and $h_{F_f(X)}=\widehat F_f(h_X)$ by functorial evaluation. At input $i$ the assertion is $\beta_{H_i}=\mathrm{id}\,\beta_{H_i}$; at a unit it is the identity. These are the two bases of this induction.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: simultaneous substitution, induction assertion and bases

proof.text:
At the outer tensor $P=T(X,Y)$ write $\beta_X^H=\beta_X(S_H)$ and $\beta_Y^H=\beta_Y(S_H)$. Primitive naturality for the child system identifications $d_X,d_Y$, followed by the two induction hypotheses, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L(d_P)\beta_{P[H]}
&=b_T(S_X(S_H),S_Y(S_H))\widehat T(\mathcal L(d_X)\beta_{X[H]},\mathcal L(d_Y)\beta_{Y[H]})\\
&=b_T(S_X(S_H),S_Y(S_H))\widehat T(\beta_X^Hh_X,\beta_Y^Hh_Y)\\
&=\beta_P(S_H)\widehat T(h_X,h_Y)
=\beta_P(S_H)h_P.
\end{aligned}$$
The first line follows by expanding $\beta_{P[H]}$ and the recursive $d_P$; the third is the recursion for $\beta_P$ and the bifunctor composition law. In particular the maps moved through $b_T$ are actual whole-system maps $d_X,d_Y$, so primitive naturality applies before taking any individual level.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: simultaneous substitution, outer tensor induction step

proof.text:
At the outer pullback $P=F_f(X)$ expand the recursion and use primitive naturality at $d_X$:
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L(d_P)\beta_{P[H]}
&=b_F(S_X(S_H))\widehat F_f(\mathcal L(d_X)\beta_{X[H]})\\
&=b_F(S_X(S_H))\widehat F_f(\beta_X(S_H)h_X)\\
&=\beta_P(S_H)\widehat F_f(h_X)
=\beta_P(S_H)h_P.
\end{aligned}$$
This proves the substitution equation for every outer expression. Naturality of the primitive comparisons used in both vertex cases is exactly naturality of the quotient realizations followed by $\mathcal LT(e,e)$ or $\mathcal LF_f(e)$. The primitive lemma states the identity moving a child system map past the counit as $e_{S'}\mathcal R\mathcal L(u)=u e_S$; thus this calculation uses that specified counit, rather than a newly chosen comparison of the same endpoints.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: simultaneous substitution, outer pullback induction step

proof.text:
For the reduction substitution equation apply counit naturality to the single whole-system isomorphism $d_P$. The substitution equation gives
$$\begin{aligned}
d_P\gamma_{P[H]}
&=d_Pe_{S_{P[H]}}\mathcal R(\beta_{P[H]})\\
&=e_{S_P(S_H)}\mathcal R\mathcal L(d_P)\mathcal R(\beta_{P[H]})\\
&=e_{S_P(S_H)}\mathcal R(\beta_P(S_H)h_P)
=\gamma_P(S_H)\mathcal R(h_P).
\end{aligned}$$
The last expression is exactly $\gamma_P(S_H)\mathcal R(K_P(\beta_{H_i})c_P)$, with its specified parentheses. Hence the flattened and iterated reduction comparisons are the same morphism in the system category.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: simultaneous substitution, reduction equation

proof.text:
For the remaining structural assertions it is convenient to write the first compatibility as $\beta_Q\widehat a=\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$, equivalent to the stated conjugation formula because $\beta_Q$ is invertible. This identity already implies the second compatibility: counit naturality at the whole-system map $a:S_P\to S_Q$ gives
$$\gamma_Q\mathcal R(\widehat a)=e_{S_Q}\mathcal R(\beta_Q\widehat a)=e_{S_Q}\mathcal R\mathcal L(a)\mathcal R(\beta_P)=a e_{S_P}\mathcal R(\beta_P)=a\gamma_P.$$
It therefore suffices to check closure of the first identity; the second will follow for each resulting structural system map by this very calculation.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: structural maps, reduction compatibility from conjugation

proof.text:
Identity maps satisfy $\beta_P\mathrm{id}=\mathcal L(\mathrm{id})\beta_P$. If $a:P\to Q$ and $b:Q\to V$ satisfy the structural identity, then
$$\beta_V(\widehat b\widehat a)=\mathcal L(b)\beta_Q\widehat a=\mathcal L(b)\mathcal L(a)\beta_P=\mathcal L(ba)\beta_P.$$
When $a$ is an isomorphism, its identity implies that $\widehat a=\beta_Q^{-1}\mathcal L(a)\beta_P$ is invertible, with inverse $\beta_P^{-1}\mathcal L(a^{-1})\beta_Q$. Thus $\beta_P\widehat a^{-1}=\mathcal L(a^{-1})\beta_Q$. These computations prove closure under identities, composable structural maps and inverses whenever defined.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: structural maps, identities, composition and inverses

proof.text:
Let $a:P\to Q$ and $b:X\to Y$ be compatible structural system maps, with completed maps $\widehat a,\widehat b$. Expanding the tensor recursion, their compatibilities and primitive naturality gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\beta_{T(Q,Y)}\widehat T(\widehat a,\widehat b)
&=b_T(S_Q,S_Y)\widehat T(\beta_Q\widehat a,\beta_Y\widehat b)\\
&=b_T(S_Q,S_Y)\widehat T(\mathcal L(a),\mathcal L(b))\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_X)\\
&=\mathcal L T(a,b)b_T(S_P,S_X)\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_X)
=\mathcal L T(a,b)\beta_{T(P,X)}.
\end{aligned}$$
For pullback the calculation is
$$\beta_{F_f(Q)}\widehat F_f(\widehat a)=b_F(S_Q)\widehat F_f(\mathcal L(a)\beta_P)=\mathcal L F_f(a)b_F(S_P)\widehat F_f(\beta_P)=\mathcal L F_f(a)\beta_{F_f(P)}.$$
Taking either tensor map to be an identity proves tensoring with an unchanged expression. Iterating these single-vertex calculations proves the assertion in any finite tensor or pullback context.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: structural maps, tensor and pullback contexts

proof.text:
For simultaneous substitution of a natural structural map $a:P\to Q$, put $B=(\beta_{H_i})_i$. Under the specified evaluation identifications the substituted maps are $a[H]=d_Q^{-1}a_{S_H}d_P$ and $\widehat a[H]=c_Q^{-1}\widehat a_{K_H}c_P$. Naturality of the completed structural map at the family $B:K_H\to\mathcal LS_H$ reads
$$K_Q(B)\widehat a_{K_H}=\widehat a_{\mathcal LS_H}K_P(B).$$
Using the already proved substitution equations on $Q$ and $P$, and the assumed structural compatibility at the normalized family $S_H$, compute
$$\begin{aligned}
\mathcal L(d_Q)\beta_{Q[H]}\widehat a[H]
&=\beta_Q(S_H)K_Q(B)\widehat a_{K_H}c_P\\
&=\beta_Q(S_H)\widehat a_{\mathcal LS_H}K_P(B)c_P\\
&=\mathcal L(a_{S_H})\beta_P(S_H)K_P(B)c_P\\
&=\mathcal L(a_{S_H}d_P)\beta_{P[H]}
=\mathcal L(d_Qa[H])\beta_{P[H]}.
\end{aligned}$$
Cancel the isomorphism $\mathcal L(d_Q)$ to get the structural compatibility after substitution. The reduction compatibility follows from step 11. Naturality here is the naturality of the structural maps under discussion, including their completed versions; it is not a claim about arbitrary assigned arrows.

source.place: Final paragraph, compatibility with coefficient passage; agent argument: structural maps, simultaneous substitution

proof.text: The inductions used no distinctness of input occurrences: for example at $T(i,i)$ both child equations use the same $v_i$ or $\beta_{H_i}$, and the bifunctor calculation remains unchanged. An expression with only units has the same unit bases and tensor or pullback steps; a context with no schemes admits no output expression and has no case to check. All recursions terminate because the trees are finite, irrespective of the size of the sets of available schemes and inputs. The closure calculations apply to total-complex tensor constraints and finite adjunction-normalized pullback compositors precisely when their primitive structural equations have been supplied, as the statement assumes. All of the established equations occur in the ordinary derived system categories and their functor images; none was deduced by detecting equality levelwise.
